pairs.subject: breach-alerting-and-attribution
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/communication/notifications.rs:38 stores an operator-supplied webhook (alert_fired is relayed to Slack/Discord/Teams/generic) with no per-channel signing secret and no https-only check, and delivery at src-tauri/src/engine/webhook_notifier.rs:425 posts unsigned, so a generic receiver cannot tell a real breach alert from any forged POST

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/webhook_notifier.rs:425 sends only User-Agent/X-Personas-Provider headers, no HMAC+timestamp over the delivered bytes; notifications.rs:38 issues no secret and accepts plaintext URLs; notifications.rs:70 echoes the sink's response body (256 chars) into the operator UI. Delivery-time private-address refusal IS present via SSRF_SAFE_HTTP at webhook_notifier.rs:419

src-tauri/src/commands/communication/observability/alerts.rs:123 create_fired_alert lets the client persist fires into the rule.id-keyed history the server evaluator reads as its cooldown, the same cross-scope suppression already recorded on overview-observability and stores-slices-overview

pairs.registryProposal: This row is marked governance: weak, but it holds the alert-rule CRUD, fired-alert persistence and the webhook-subscription door (alerts.rs, notifications.rs), so the subject genuinely governs it; the weak flag understates the match. Separately, the evaluator itself (src-tauri/src/commands/execution/alert_evaluator.rs) is the file most governed by this subject and should be checked for a pair on whichever context owns it.
